technical_and_design_decisions: User stories are implemented as distinct but related features within the Spring Cloud Data (s-c-d) and Spring Cloud Stream Modules (s-c-s-m) codebases.
For U1 (CLI for REST APIs), will use Spring Shell for the command-line interface and a REST client like Spring's RestTemplate or WebClient to interact with the StreamController endpoints.
For U2 (Redis counter adaptation), will refactor existing XD counter code to align with the s-c-s module and programming model, likely using Spring Data Redis for connectivity.
For U3 and U8 (CI setup), will configure GitHub Actions as the CI system, leveraging the existing Gradle build infrastructure.
For U4 (JAR resolution for Boot loader), will implement a custom module dependency resolver that can parse module manifests and integrate with Spring Boot's executable JAR class loading mechanism.
For U5 (Bootify ModuleLauncher), will refactor the existing ModuleLauncher to use Spring Boot's application context, property sources, and command-line argument parsing, making it a Boot application.
For U6 (PHD/HDFS investigation), will perform a spike investigation (proof-of-concept) rather than a full implementation, focusing on classpath management and dependency isolation.
For U7 (REST for stream commands), will design and implement new REST controller endpoints in the s-c-d server to expose stream management operations, using existing service layer components.
assumptions: The developer has intermediate to advanced familiarity with the Spring ecosystem (Spring Boot, Spring Shell, Spring Data), Java build tools (Gradle), and CI/CD concepts.
The existing s-c-d and s-c-s-m codebases are accessible and have a modular structure that allows for incremental changes.
For activities involving investigation (U6) or setting up new infrastructure (U3, U8), time includes analysis, configuration, documentation of steps, and basic validation.
Testing effort includes writing necessary unit and integration tests to ensure the new code functions correctly within the existing test framework.
Time estimates account for code reviews, iterations based on review feedback, and minor debugging within the activity.
Communication and coordination overhead with other team members is minimal, as the spec defines the scope per story.
External dependencies and libraries (e.g., specific Redis client versions, Spring Cloud dependencies) are already available in the project's dependency management.

activities.activity_description: Analyze StreamController REST endpoints and design the Spring Shell commands and underlying client logic to invoke them.
Implement the Spring Shell commands, REST client integration, and write unit/integration tests for the new CLI functionality.
Analyze the existing XD Redis counter implementation and the target s-c-s module architecture to plan the adaptation.
Refactor and implement the Redis counter as a s-c-s compatible module, including configuration and integration tests.
Configure GitHub Actions workflow for the s-c-d repository, including build, test, and basic reporting steps.
Design the mechanism to parse module dependency metadata (e.g., from a manifest) and resolve JARs.
Implement the dependency resolver and integrate it with the Spring Boot loader's classpath handling for modules.
Analyze the current ModuleLauncher to identify parts to be replaced or enhanced by Spring Boot's application context and properties.
Refactor ModuleLauncher to extend a Spring Boot application, adding property support and writing tests.
Spike investigation: analyze PHD dependencies, HDFS module requirements, and prototype a classpath/isolation approach.
Design the new REST endpoints for stream commands, including request/response DTOs and controller structure.
Implement the REST controllers, wire them to existing services, and write integration tests.
Configure GitHub Actions workflow for the spring-cloud-stream-modules (s-c-s-m) repository.
